title: Warn when a disk is fuller than a set limit
summary: A small script reads how full a disk is and reports a warning when it passes your limit, for example 85 percent. Run it by hand, or from a timer or cron job, to hear about a filling disk before it is full.

steps.explain: Save the script from the script section as ~/bin/disk-warn.sh, then make it executable.
Look at the current fill level of the disk you want to watch.
steps.expect: A line with the Use% column for that mount point.

placeholders.name: MOUNT_POINT
placeholders.description: Folder where the disk or partition is mounted

steps.explain: Test the warning with a low limit so that it fires. The script prints a WARNING line and returns exit code 2. Normal use is the next step.

placeholders.name: MOUNT_POINT
placeholders.description: Folder where the disk or partition is mounted

steps.explain: Real check with your limit, here 85 percent. The popup appears only when the script exits with a non-zero code, which means the disk is above the limit.
steps.expect: 'OK: /home is NN% full (limit 85%)' and no popup when the disk is fine.

placeholders.name: MOUNT_POINT
placeholders.description: Folder where the disk or partition is mounted

steps.explain: Run the check on a schedule. Put the same command in a systemd user timer or a cron line that runs every hour.

script.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
# Print a warning line when a filesystem is fuller than THRESHOLD percent.
# Exit status 0 = below threshold, 2 = at or above threshold (usable from cron or a timer).
# Usage: disk-warn.sh MOUNT_POINT [THRESHOLD]
MOUNT="${1:?usage: $0 MOUNT_POINT [THRESHOLD]}"
LIMIT="${2:-85}"
USED=$(df --output=pcent "$MOUNT" | tail -n 1 | tr -dc '0-9')
if (( USED >= LIMIT )); then
  echo "WARNING: $MOUNT is ${USED}% full (limit ${LIMIT}%)" >&2
  exit 2
fi
echo "OK: $MOUNT is ${USED}% full (limit ${LIMIT}%)"
